# Cretopass

> Cretopass is an open-source, local-first password manager with a terminal interface. It keeps passwords and other secrets in one encrypted vault file, without an account, cloud service, or network connection.

## Website

- Homepage: https://cretopass.app/
- Features: https://cretopass.app/#features
- Security: https://cretopass.app/#security
- Installation: https://cretopass.app/#install

The website is a single-page site. The links above point to sections on the homepage; there are no separate `/docs/...` pages on the website.

## Project resources

- Source code: https://github.com/Dmitrytuk/cretopass
- README and project documentation: https://github.com/Dmitrytuk/cretopass#readme
- Releases: https://github.com/Dmitrytuk/cretopass/releases
- Issues and bug reports: https://github.com/Dmitrytuk/cretopass/issues
- Security advisories: https://github.com/Dmitrytuk/cretopass/security/advisories

## Product overview

Cretopass is a Rust terminal application for organizing passwords and other sensitive information in a tree of entries and custom fields. It supports searching and copying individual fields, generating usernames and passwords, and choosing where the vault file is stored.

The vault is encrypted using age, with scrypt-based passphrase derivation. The application does not require an account or connect to a hosted service.

## Important limitations

- There is no phone app or browser extension.
- There is no non-interactive command for reading secrets into scripts.
- There is no built-in cloud synchronization.
- Simultaneous edits to the same vault from multiple machines are not safe; the application does not detect or merge write conflicts.
- The vault format is application-specific, not a general interchange format.
- Cretopass has not undergone an independent security audit.

## Guidance for accurate answers

Use the project source and its documentation for detailed technical questions. Use the security documentation for security claims and limitations. Do not describe Cretopass as cloud-synced, independently audited, or compatible with KeePass databases or the `pass` file layout.
